stills.title: Opening wide view

The camera has moved toward the tool since the first panel; the apparent size change is part of that approach, not a growing tool. Freeze before the macro pulse explanation. Retain enough housing to locate the sensor on the same instrument. stills.title: Outgoing pulse
stills.provenance: T049 JPEG decoded from selected v011 movie; native mapping recorded in image-manifest.json
stills.selection_reason: Match the extreme close-up: the large circular sensor occupies the right side and the rock wall is to the left across the clearance. Freeze the outward-travelling cyan wavefronts between sensor and wall, at the exact positions and curvature shown. The pulse has left the sensor and is travelling toward the left-hand wall; this panel precedes the return. Preserve the count and spacing of the visible arcs. The cyan lines explain otherwise invisible acoustics: use delicate controlled luminosity, not solid wires, sparks or a laser beam. Keep both the sensor boundary and the wavefronts crisp.

stills.title: Returning echo
stills.provenance: T049 JPEG decoded from selected v011 movie; native mapping recorded in image-manifest.json
stills.selection_reason: Match the same sensor close-up, now at the return phase. Small green echo arcs sit immediately to the left of the circular sensor, travelling back toward it after the wall response. Preserve the faint traces farther toward the wall exactly where present in the reference; do not add a new outgoing pulse or wall-impact explosion. This freezes the return just before arrival. Match the preceding panel's steel, rock, lighting, scale and optical character so the change in signal state is clear.

stills.title: Recorded wall develops
stills.selection_reason: Match the diagonal medium-wide view, with the lower tool toward bottom-left and the pipe continuing toward top-right. The camera is pulling back and changing viewing angle. Freeze the partially revealed blue recorded-wall pattern around and above the sensor region: a patchwork of translucent cells and thin contours, with the incomplete advancing boundary at the same location as in the reference. This reveals previously recorded information, not rock being manufactured or new measurements everywhere. Keep the tool physically opaque beneath the informational overlay, with the cutaway and borehole relationships intact. Show brighter newly revealed cells and calmer settled cells without thick neon cages.

stills.title: Full recorded-history reveal
stills.selection_reason: Match the final wide diagonal view: the complete visible tool lies toward bottom-left and the long connected pipe extends toward top-right. The pullback has revealed the longer interval of stored history. Freeze the settled blue translucent cell/contour display along the borehole at the reference's exact extent. The information remains a restrained overlay separate from physical rock and opaque metal. Preserve the open lower end and all visible geometry as shown, without inventing a bit or cap. Use deeper focus to read the full progression from local sensor to the long recorded interval. Keep the same materials, palette and lighting as every preceding panel.
